issues.problem: Fig 6·d, its caption and Check-yourself answer 2 say Discord uses 'the same 41 bits' from 2015, lasting to about 2084. issues.problem: The prose narrates the recording and the teacher instead of stating things, which is lec01's issue 14 again. Examples: '(The recording garbles the lecture's exact words here; that reflex is the sense of it.)'; 'When someone tells the instructor their database is slow, the first thing he checks…'; 'the team that built Amazon's ID service sat right next to him'; 'In 2016, bored at Amazon and heavily into MongoDB, the instructor wrote…'; 'the class board crossed it out at the crash, and the lecture counted both 8 and 9 as leaked'; 'One idea raised in class'; 'The lecture describes it as living on the heap'; 'As worked out in class'; the fig-3-2 label 'strictly monotonic, as the lecture says it'.
issues.fix: Delete the recording-garbled aside. Rewrite teacher biography as plain claims ('A common first check for a slow database is index size'; 'Amazon described the design in a public tech talk'; 'A 2016 benchmark (arpitbhayani.me) measured…'). Change 'raised in class' to 'One tempting idea'. Leave provenance to the meta lines and the 'Redrawn from the class board' captions. Relabel fig-3-2 as 'strictly monotonic'.
issues.recheck: Resolved on the current pages. Every example named in the first critique and in the previous final look is gone: both garbled-recording asides (§1.1, §5.2 'the exact words are lost in the recording'), 'the instructor's first check' (§4.3 now 'From the lecture's own practice: when a database is slow, check index size first'), the Amazon-team biography, 'The lecture learned it from a blog post', 'The class sketched thousands of them' (Fig 7·b caption now 'Thousands of them on "say, 10 or 15" servers', fig/1440-light-fig-7b.png), '(The lecture spoke of losing both 8 and 9 …)' (§2.6 now 'Had the crash come before 8 went out, both 8 and 9 would be lost', sweep/1440-light/2-building-getid/012.png), 'living on the heap' (now a plain analogy with a cppreference note), and the fig-3-2 label reads 'strictly monotonic' (fig/1440-light-fig-3-2.png). Mentions of the lecture, class or instructor across the lec03 sources are now 58 against 84 in the Lecture 1 reference, and most of what is left attributes an opinion ('in the lecture's view'), as lec01 does. The Jeff Dean story sits in a collapsed 'skip unless you like war stories' aside (sweep/1440-light/3-order-and-clocks/006.png), where narration is in place. Four leftover narrating spots are logged as C-18 (low).
